heroLead: Chalkhill sits along the old National Road corridor in Fayette County, where family land often carries mineral interests nobody in the house has looked at since a grandparent's estate closed.
intro: Chalkhill is a small crossroads community, not a town with its own courthouse, so most of what we hear from owners here starts with a deed that was recorded in Uniontown decades ago and never revisited. Fayette County's mineral history runs deeper than Marcellus. This was coke country long before horizontal drilling, and a lot of the severed mineral interests around Chalkhill trace back to coal and coke transactions from the early 1900s, with oil and gas rights split off separately, sometimes to a different party entirely.

If you're holding a fractional interest that shows up on a Fayette County tax bill you can't quite make sense of, or a royalty check that's shrunk to almost nothing, we buy those interests directly. No listing process, no waiting for a broker to find a buyer.

sections.heading: Where Chalkhill Sits on the Map
paragraphs: Chalkhill is on the western flank of the Marcellus wet-gas fairway, closer to the edge of the core than deep Washington or Greene County acreage. That doesn't mean the ground is worthless, but it does mean activity here has been more selective, tied to specific operator programs rather than blanket development. Some Chalkhill-area tracts also carry legacy shallow rights from the older Fayette County oil fields that predate Marcellus by a century.

Because this is flank acreage, offers on Chalkhill minerals can vary a lot depending on which pool of gas is being targeted and whether a nearby unit has actually produced. We look at recent activity in your section before we ever quote a number.

sections.heading: Split Estates and Old Coke-Era Deeds
paragraphs: A lot of Fayette County land was severed for coal and coke rights first, with oil and gas reserved or conveyed in a separate transaction. That means the surface, the coal, and the gas can belong to three different people, and the paperwork proving which one you inherited is sometimes buried in a probate file from the 1940s or 50s. We've walked enough of these chains of title to know what to ask the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds for, and we do that legwork ourselves rather than asking you to.
If your family's copy of the deed is missing or unreadable, that's normal, not a dead end. We can usually reconstruct the chain from public record before we ever ask you for anything.

sections.heading: Deductions on a Small Royalty Check
paragraphs: Owners with fractional interests near Chalkhill often tell us the same thing: the check used to be a few hundred dollars a quarter and now it's a fraction of that after gathering, compression, and marketing fees get taken off the top. Post-production cost deductions are legal in Pennsylvania unless your lease specifically bars them, and most old leases from this era don't. We can walk through your statement with you and tell you honestly whether the deductions look normal for this play or worth a second look.

faqs.question: Is Chalkhill part of the core Marcellus play?
faqs.answer: It's on the flank, not the deep core. Activity depends on the specific unit and operator, which is exactly why we check recent permitting near your tract before quoting anything.

faqs.question: My deed only mentions coal, not gas. Do I still own minerals?
faqs.answer: Possibly, depending on how the original severance was worded. Old Fayette County coke-era deeds sometimes reserved oil and gas separately from coal. We'll pull the chain of title and tell you plainly what we find.

faqs.question: What if I can't find my grandparents' original mineral deed?
faqs.answer: That's common. Deeds this old are recorded at the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds in Uniontown, and we can usually locate and verify the chain ourselves before asking you for paperwork.

faqs.question: Will you buy a small fractional interest that barely produces income?
faqs.answer: Yes. Small, fractional, flank-acreage interests are a lot of what we buy. We'd rather give you a fair cash number now than have you carry a tiny royalty check for another twenty years.
